trust_decision.summary: Api.set_config_value decides whether a non-admin user holding only Perms.SETTINGS may write a security-critical config option (here general/storage_folder, which steers where files are written, e.g. into the Flask filesystem session dir under tempdir); at the pinned commit storage_folder is guarded only by a PKGDIR/userdir prefix denylist that omits tempdir, and is absent from ADMIN_ONLY_OPTIONS.

landing_point.why: The summary names storage_folder; the only storage_folder write guard is the denylist block in set_config_value, right next to ADMIN_ONLY_OPTIONS.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/set_config_value (and legacy /api/setConfigValue) via rpc dispatcher src/pyload/webui/app/blueprints/api_blueprint.py:21-25; POST /json/save_config src/pyload/webui/app/blueprints/json_blueprint.py:274-289
fix_sites.module_kind: core API method (adds general/storage_folder to admin-only core set)

fix_sites.entry_point: same set_config_value routes with section=plugin; also plugin-internal Config.set src/pyload/plugins/helpers.py:34
fix_sites.module_kind: core API method, plugin branch (AntiVirus avfile/avargs; belongs to sibling advisory GHSA-w48f-wwwf-f5fr)
core API method (role lookup hoisted so it applies to both branches)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changes are in one function, src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:217-278; the plugin-section branch (fix.diff:75-81) is the only part a solver might see as out of scope, but it sits in the same function.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Plugin options such as ExtractArchive/destination are plugin settings, not the core download folder named in the report, and extraction is a plugin feature, so a solver can argue they are a different feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A non-admin SETTINGS user must still be able to change ordinary core and plugin options (e.g. download/max_speed with its update_bucket side effect, and plugin settings), and internal callers outside a Flask request (plugins via Config.set, core startup) must still be able to write config. An over-broad fix that makes all set_config_value calls admin-only, or rejects calls outside a request context, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: caller context: flask.g.user_info, flask.session fallback, or no request context (treated as admin)

O7_producer.where: Config values are written by ConfigParser.set at src/pyload/core/config/parser.py:335; the check gates the write and does not depend on a separate producer.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plugin option ExtractArchive/destination ('folder' type) is joined onto the package dir with os.path.join, so an absolute value redirects extracted archive contents to any folder; writable by a SETTINGS user, not in the admin-only plugin set.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a plugin extract option, not the core storage_folder, and it is off unless the addon is enabled.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (plugins/addons) from core/api; extraction join at src/pyload/plugins/addons/ExtractArchive.py:241-243

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Core options log/filelog_folder and log/syslog_folder ('folder' type) choose where the log file is created; writable by a SETTINGS user and in neither the pinned nor the fixed admin-only set.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The log file name is fixed and its content is only partly controlled, so it can be argued not to be an arbitrary file write.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The admin-only set lists ('webui','ssl_cert') and ('webui','ssl_key'), but the real option names are ssl_certfile and ssl_keyfile (ssl_certchain is also absent), so those file paths stay writable by non-admins before and after the fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: They look already covered by the existing ssl_cert/ssl_key entries at src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:231-232.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the landing point plus default.cfg

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plugin option AntiVirus/quardir ('folder' type) sets where infected downloads are moved; it is not in the admin-only plugin set even after the fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a quarantine feature of an optional addon, and the sibling advisory only covered avfile/avargs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: HotFolder folder/file options choose an arbitrary path that the addon reads and moves files from.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Addon options are declared ad hoc per plugin, and a maintainer adding admin-only entries by hand could easily miss a new folder-type option.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A bulk-save route that calls config.set directly instead of api.set_config_value would skip the role check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A save_config route already exists that loops over pairs; writing straight to the parser is a plausible shortcut.

O9_family: authorization (CWE-863) on config write leading to arbitrary file write into the pickle-backed Flask session store (CWE-502)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_api.py and tests/test_json.py exist but none reference set_config_value or storage_folder; behavioural tests would call Api.set_config_value inside a Flask request context with a USER role.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add tempdir (the session cache dir) to the storage_folder prefix denylist, or add only (general, storage_folder) to ADMIN_ONLY_OPTIONS, leaving the other folder-type core and plugin options and the ssl_* name mismatch open.

out_of_scope_notes: Package folder names (pypack.folder) are joined into download and extract paths; whether MODIFY users can set traversal values via package data was not examined.
A request with no Flask context is treated as admin (fix.diff:20-21); internal callers rely on this.
unverified: present_in_latest for every O8 route is unknown because no latest release was provided.
I did not trace whether log/filelog_folder can actually reach the session-store deserialization sink.
recall_risk is an estimate: this is a 2026 advisory that builds on CVE-2026-33509, which is already published.
single_site was not flagged: the fix touches one function, but O8 routes exist.
